skills/github/scripts/add-finding.sh:54 | The edit and the comment are two writes, and nothing marks that the section is in the body already. Run the script again after a stop between them, and it appends the same `## Also:` section a second time and raises `also:` by one. | The first run's `gh issue edit` succeeds and `gh issue comment` fails (network, HTTP 502, rate limit). The script exits non-zero, so the agent or the person runs it again. The host had `also: 0`, so the check lets the second run through and the body gets two copies. Not sure how often a run stops at exactly that point.
skills/github/scripts/collect.sh:136 | `has()` matches `^==> (PR )?#N ` on any line of the file, and issue bodies and comments are copied into the file as they are. So a body that quotes an entry line makes `bodies` and `entries` skip a number that has no entry of its own. | Issue #7's body pastes collect.sh output with the line `==> #5 The scout misses …`. Later `bodies <file> 5` prints `already in the file: #5` and fetches nothing. This is likely in this repo, because its issues are about the scout and its file.
skills/github/scout.md:40 | The scout is told that an entry ends at the next line that starts with `==`. Markdown bodies often have such lines, so the scout cuts an entry early, or takes the rest of a body for a new section or entry. | A body with a setext H1 (`Title` with `=====` under it), a pasted `== Search:` block, or a line `==> …`. The rest of that body and its comments are then read as a different part. Not sure how a model reads it in practice, but the rule as written gives the wrong boundary.
skills/github/scripts/worktree.sh:47 | When gh lists a linked branch whose ref was deleted, the line has an empty name. If that line comes first, `branch` becomes empty. Then `git for-each-ref refs/heads/` matches every local branch, and the script prints "checked out already" with the path of whatever worktree comes first, such as the main checkout. | `gh issue develop --list` on an issue whose first linked branch was deleted. collect.sh and the test fixture both handle `linkedBranches` nodes with `ref: null`, so these nodes do occur. I assume gh's `ListLinkedBranches` turns a null `Ref` into `BranchName: ""` and prints `\t…/tree/`. I did not check that in gh's source.
skills/github/scripts/worktree.sh:73 | The fallback for older gh fetches from the remote named `origin`. But `gh issue develop` creates the branch on gh's base repository, and that can be a different remote. In that case the fetch fails, or `git worktree add` finds no `origin/<branch>`. | A fork checkout: `origin` is the fork, `upstream` is the parent, and gh resolves to `upstream` (by default order or by `gh repo set-default`), with gh older than the version that has `--worktree`. The same mismatch is in take-in-check.sh:19. The old text said "this checkout's `origin`", but the script compares with gh's base repo, so an issue URL on `origin` gets "stop" in a fork.
skills/github/scripts/take-in-check.sh:62 | A refusal exits 1, and a failed `gh` call under `set -e` also exits 1. SKILL.md:95-98 tells the agent to handle these two outcomes differently ("wait" for a refusal, "report the error and stop" for an error), but the exit code cannot tell them apart. add-finding.sh:28 has the same problem. | `take-in-check.sh 9` where #9 is a pull request: GraphQL gives "Could not resolve to an Issue", which is exit 1 with nothing on stdout. Also any HTTP 502 or auth failure. An agent that uses only the exit code reads this as "wait". This is minor if the agent always reads stderr.
